title: Self-Publishing a Book: Which Freelancers You Need and When
h1: Self-publishing a book: which freelancers you need and when
description: The stages of self-publishing and which freelancers help at each: editing, beta readers, proofreading, cover, interior layout, audiobook and marketing.
intro: Self-publishing gives authors full control, but it also means doing the work a publisher would normally arrange: editing, design, formatting and marketing. Freelancers can fill each of these roles, but the order matters. Hiring a cover designer before the manuscript is ready, or proofreading before editing, wastes money. This article explains the stages in a sensible order and what each freelancer does.

faq.q: Do I really need an editor?
faq.a: Almost every book benefits from professional editing. It is the most important investment for quality.

faq.q: What is the difference between editing and proofreading?
faq.a: Editing improves structure and language; proofreading catches final errors after layout.

faq.q: When should I hire a cover designer?
faq.a: Once the manuscript is close to final and you know the length and format.

faq.q: Do ebooks and print books need different files?
faq.a: Yes. Print needs a fixed layout and a full cover; ebooks need reflowable files.

faq.q: Can I publish an audiobook too?
faq.a: Yes. Check each platform's rules on narration before you start.
